reason: The curved canals and turning sensors seem to form the head-turning detector needed for balance.
expectation: I expect a fluid-filled turning sensor, though I am unsure how its signal connects to eye movement yet.

alternatives.reason: Tilt and acceleration sensors also support the goal, but I chose to follow head turning first.

effect: The canals sense changes in head rotation through fluid movement; I will build the other balance sensors next.
reaction: The fluid bending the sensors makes the connection clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should add sensing for tilt and acceleration.
expectation: I expect balance organs that detect tilt and acceleration using the weighted membranes.

effect: The weighted membranes help sense gravity and changes in straight-line motion, completing the other type of balance sensor.
reaction: The comparison between tipping and moving forward makes their role clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should bring the two kinds of balance sensors together.
expectation: I expect a combined set of balance organs sensing rotation, gravity and straight-line acceleration.

effect: The rotation and gravity sensors are now grouped as balance organs beside the cochlea; the next step is to connect them.
reaction: The grouping is straightforward, though it adds little explanation.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect the sensors to the brainstem.
expectation: I expect balance organs connected by nerves to the brainstem, with reflex connections still to add.

effect: The balance organs now have nerves leading toward the brainstem, ready to connect to the body.
reaction: The connection is clear, though the result adds little explanation.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should add the balance organs to the body.
expectation: I expect the body to gain connected balance organs, with reflex connections still to add.

effect: The balance organs are now connected to the body's brainstem, leaving the reflex connections to add.
reaction: The placement is clear, though it adds little explanation.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect balance signals to eye and posture controls.
expectation: I expect the body to gain reflex pathways that help stabilize the eyes and posture during head movement.

effect: The completed reflex connections show how balance signals help steady the eyes and adjust posture, alongside vision and information from joints and muscles.
reaction: The opposite eye movement was a satisfying, concrete payoff for the earlier connections.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the reflex connections was most worthwhile because the result connected head movement to steady vision and posture in a relatable situation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grouping the sensors and then connecting them to nerves and the body felt repetitive; those results added little explanation beyond their names and pictures.

surprise.text: I had not expected the eyes to turn opposite the head to keep the view steady.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the separate assembly steps felt mechanical because each had only one offered combination.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in another chapter if it offered another concrete explanation like the eye reflex, but the repeated assembly steps make me hesitant.
